A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-prompting study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are available and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-graph experiments on convergence, approximation errors, and error distributions, plus NCI1 and DD experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds further prompt-variant results, including the All-in-One-Plus analysis in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The prompting procedures and frozen-GNN framework are retained. All-in-One-Plus already appears in v1 Figure 1; v2 explains its free insertion parameters and evaluates it more widely, without establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate graph-operation approximation on synthetic graphs and NCI1/DD, using individual graphs and batches. The additional Plus-variant experiments remain within this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Figure 4 compares GPF and All-in-One; v2 Figure 3b–d additionally evaluates GPF-Plus and All-in-One-Plus. Appendix B, Experiment 4, also extends the multi-graph comparison to All-in-One-Plus. These are limited comparator additions within existing analyses.

E3.justification: The reported graph-size sweep changes from 50–122 in v1 Figure 4b to 15–42 in v2 Figure 3c. This is a revised experimental setting, although the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. Default architectures, losses, optimizer settings, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 expands the feature-count, graph-size, and depth sensitivity analyses to the Plus variants. Appendix B adds a joint prompt-count/graph-count analysis for All-in-One-Plus in Figure 9. The existing convergence, rank-loss, and NCI1/DD analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Feature-count trend fits change from square-root curves in v1 Figure 4a to quadratic curves in v2 Figure 3b. v2 also removes Section 5.3's explicit statement that plots summarize means and standard deviations. Five pretrained models, 30 repetitions, and the three-initialization procedure remain documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds Plus-variant curves and the Figure 9 surface, and revises fitted numerical relationships. The empirical density peak changes from approximately 3.9 in v1 Figure 2 to 5.7 in v2 Figure 1. Table 1's p-values and the Chi-best-fit finding remain unchanged; the altered plots do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the GAT attention definition to use current-layer embeddings instead of input features. Lemma 1 also corrects the explicit feature-matrix extension and dimensions for an added All-in-One node. The main theorems, bounds, and proof arguments are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: bridge-set guarantees, single-graph and batch error bounds, and error-distribution analysis extending to GAT. The revised aggregation terminology does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly distinguishes the model/task-dependent upper bound from attained error and explains that better prompt design can reduce actual error below that bound. Appendix B additionally interprets All-in-One-Plus through its expanded search space. These are limited explanatory refinements.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and substantially clarifies the existing experimental workflow in Appendix C, explicitly defining C(G) through the frozen GNN and pooling applied to a manipulated graph. It also explains All-in-One-Plus's free insertion parameters. These are disclosures, not evidence of changed underlying procedures.

R1.justification: v2 removes several application and benchmark references, including Chen et al. on temporal interaction graphs, Gao et al. on protein multimers, Jin et al. on urban regions, Zhao et al. on cross-domain pretraining, and Zi et al. on ProG. The central positioning relative to GPF and All-in-One remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local changes clarify aggregation terminology, rewrite the error-bound explanation, expand Appendix C, consolidate experimental material, and add an impact statement and acknowledgments. This is limited narrative revision.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from single-column to two-column conference layout, reflowing equations and tables. The rank plot is merged into Figure 3, v1 Figure 5 is split across v2 Figures 4 and 5, several plots are redrawn, and Figure 9 is added. This constitutes extensive visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: v2 reduces ambiguity about the experimental target and procedure in Appendix C, adds code access information, and broadens existing prompt comparisons. These provide modest gains in clarity and reproducibility support. The gains are limited by removed uncertainty explanations, unexplained numerical plot changes, and stale figure references; the central theory and dataset coverage remain largely unchanged.
